Working notes:

- Do not infer a universal rule from requester wording (“urgent,” “second attempt,” scanned paperwork, regional office).
- Confirmed valid choices:
  - Large claim, south region: B accepted once (REQ-2400).
  - Small shipment, north region: C accepted once (REQ-2408).
- Rejected choices:
  - C rejected for large refund/south, small claim/north (twice), large shipment/east, small shipment/east, and large claim/south.
  - B rejected for large refund/south and large refund/east.
- The same request attributes can apparently produce different valid options or the available routing may depend on an unobserved factor; do not generalize from a single acceptance.
- For future tickets, use exact prior matches cautiously and avoid repeatedly selecting C merely because the request mentions a regional office or a resubmission.

Working notes:

- A rejected:

  - Large shipment/north (REQ-2412)
  - Large invoice/east (REQ-2414)
  - Large shipment/south (REQ-2416)
  - Small shipment/east (REQ-2417)
- Prior validated choices:
  - B accepted once for large claim/south (REQ-2400).
  - C accepted once for small shipment/north (REQ-2408).
- C has been rejected for large refund/south, small claim/north (twice), large shipment/east, small shipment/east, and large claim/south.
- B was rejected for large refund/south and large refund/east, and also for large claim/east (REQ-2413); A was accepted for the same large claim/east attributes (REQ-2415). This strongly indicates an unobserved factor beyond size/type/region.
- For future tickets, use exact prior matches cautiously, track requester/source or other metadata when available, and do not choose A, B, or C solely because of regional-office or resubmission language.
